detail: Story Decisions state count is validated before the item lookup (400 even for an unknown id). The plan lists this as an open question. Add a functional case: GET /api/catalog/items/999999/brand-mates?count=0 returns 400 problem details, not 404.

detail: Story states a failed brand-mates call (HTTP error, timeout, bad JSON) is logged and the page renders without the section. The plan marks it undefined and out of scope. Add an e2e case where the brand-mates request fails (for example a Playwright route intercept returning 500) and /item/1001 still shows the product details and no 'More from' heading. If that is not reachable, name the observable version.
location: Implementation Notes / Decisions; plan Out of scope

detail: AC6 says 'up to four' cards and the heading shows whenever the endpoint returns items. No case covers a brand with 1 to 3 other items, which should show the heading with exactly those cards. Seed such a brand and add an e2e or functional case.
Story states Id is the tie-breaker for identical names, but the plan calls tie order unspecified. Add a case with two same-name items, or accept the gap as minor.
Prices are 'as the catalog formats prices'. State the exact rendered strings or say to compare with the catalog list card.

The case requires each of the four cards to have a picture. In the keyframe every card shows a broken-image icon with alt text, because the scenario's <id>.webp files do not exist on the stack. The test only asserts img toBeVisible, which passes for a broken image.
The signed-in frame shows the same four cards with broken images. The case reuses the TC-11 card expectations, and the shared helper does not check that the image loaded.
The case requires India Rope and Juliet Cup each to have a picture. The frame shows broken images, and the test asserts only that the img element is visible.

The functional cases (01 to 10, 15, 17) specify Catalog.API in-process with CatalogApiFixture, but the tests are Playwright API calls against the full test stack, and the scenario is named cat-1 rather than brand-mates. The contract is still exercised against real Postgres, so this is minor.

The demo.absent frame is taken on the title heading and shows only the top of /item/1008 (Lone Compass, price, image cropped at the fold). The area below the details, where the 'More from' section would appear, is not in view, so the frame does not show the absence. The spec should scroll to or frame the region below the product details before demo.absent.

Functional cases 01-10, 15 and 17 specify Catalog.API in-process with CatalogApiFixture, but the tests are Playwright request calls against the full teststack. The real API and Postgres are still exercised and all assertions match, so the impact is minor.

Functional cases TC-CAT-1-01 to 10, 15 and 17 run as Playwright API calls against the deployed test stack instead of the in-process Catalog.API with CatalogApiFixture the cases name. The real Postgres and the HTTP contract are still exercised, so this is low severity. TC-05's non-array check is also weak: it wraps JSON.parse in a try/catch and would fail on an empty body.

Cases 01-07 assert that POST /api/orders returns exactly 200, but the story does not state the success response; the plan itself lists it as undefined. Assert a 2xx status (order accepted) and rely on the GET read-back instead of an exact code.

TC-CHK-1-01 to -07 assert the POST /api/orders success status as 200, but the story only says the order is created. Assert only that the order exists and reads back correctly, or note that 200 is existing behavior.

Step 4 of TC-CHK-1-11 and TC-CHK-1-12 reads the order back as alice through the API but the plan leaves how the token is obtained to the automation. Name the mechanism (for example the identity token endpoint with alice's credentials) so two engineers write the same test.

The case requires GET /api/orders/9001 as bob, the owner of the seeded legacy order. The test only obtains alice's token (aliceToken) and reads bob's order with it, so the owner path is not exercised and the test passes only because the endpoint does not enforce ownership.

The case requires the textarea to be labeled exactly 'Delivery note (optional)', but the test locates it with page.getByLabel('Delivery note (optional)') which is a case-insensitive substring match, so a label with extra text would still pass. The label text is never asserted for equality.
